get_book.description: Get one book by id, with its ISBN, publisher, page count, release date, and the ids of its characters and POV narrators.
get_book.name: get_book

parameters.description: Pick a book, or reference one from an earlier step by its id or by one of the API's book URLs (an entry from a character's 'books', say).
parameters.name: book_id

author_names.description: The same authors with blank entries dropped, ready to join into a line.

authors.description: The authors, as the API sent them.

character_count.description: How many characters appear in the book.

character_ids.description: The same characters as ids, so a workflow can feed one straight into 'Get a character' without slicing a URL apart.

characters.description: The API URL of every character who appears in the book.

country.description: Where it was published, e.g. 'United States'.

id.description: The book's id, taken from the end of its URL. The API publishes no id field of its own; this is what the other book actions take.

isbn.description: The ISBN-13 that identifies this edition.

mediaType.description: The format of this edition, e.g. 'Hardcover'.

name.description: The book's title, e.g. 'A Game of Thrones'.

numberOfPages.description: How many pages this edition runs to.

povCharacters.description: The API URL of every character who narrates a chapter of it.

pov_character_count.description: How many characters narrate a chapter of it.

pov_character_ids.description: The same POV characters as ids.

release_date.description: The same release as a plain calendar date, e.g. '1996-08-01'.

release_year.description: The year it was released, e.g. 1996.

released.description: When it was released, as the API sends it: a timestamp with no timezone, e.g. '1996-08-01T00:00:00'.

url.description: The book's own API URL, e.g. '.../api/books/1'.

get_book_pov_characters.description: Get the characters who narrate a book, as whole records rather than the URLs the book carries: who they are, what they are called, whether they are alive, and who played them on screen. The book lists its narrators as links, so this does the per-narrator lookups in one step, up to the limit you set.
get_book_pov_characters.display_str_template: Get the POV characters of Ice and Fire book {0}.

get_character_relations.description: Get a character together with their father, mother, spouse and the houses they are sworn to, all resolved into whole records in one step. description: Look up the world of A Song of Ice and Fire - and of HBO's Game of Thrones - using An API of Ice and Fire, the free, keyless, community database of the books. Search the books by title or release date, the characters by name, culture, gender, birth, death or whether they are still alive, and the houses by region, words, seats, titles, ancestral weapons or whether they have died out. Fetch any single record by id, or take the shortcuts the raw endpoints do not offer: the narrators of a book, a character's parents, spouse and allegiances, or a house's lord, heir, founder and sworn members, each resolved in one step. No account or API key required. Disclaimer: this is an independent integration with the community-run An API of Ice and Fire (anapioficeandfire.com), created by Joakim Skoog. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by George R. R. Martin, Bantam Books, Penguin Random House, or HBO; A Song of Ice and Fire, Game of Thrones and all related names, characters and trademarks are the property of their respective owners.
